instruction: I accidentally trashed a party poster. Please undelete it and put it back on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: [ -f /home/user/Desktop/poster_party_night.webp ] && echo 'File exists.' || echo 'File does not exist.'

metadata.explanation: Task requires undeleting/recovering file from Trash back to Desktop. Paraphrased instruction using 'undelete' terminology. Evaluator uses existing exact_match metric and vm_command_line getter.
metadata.verification: Verified that evaluator checks file exists at Desktop location after recovery. Uses same pattern as original with different wording.

llm_judge_reasons: Correct state extraction: The vm_command_line getter uses a bash test to check if the file exists at the exact expected path (/home/user/Desktop/poster_party_night.webp)
Appropriate metric: exact_match is suitable for this binary verification (file exists or does not exist)
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies the core requirement - that the trashed file has been restored to the Desktop
Correct expected value: 'File exists.\n' matches the actual output of the bash command when the file exists
Sound logic: The bash test [ -f ... ] && echo 'File exists.' || echo 'File does not exist.' correctly handles both success and failure cases

Semantically sufficient: While the evaluator only checks file existence (not content integrity), this is appropriate because the setup explicitly trashes the file and the only way to restore it is through the trash recovery mechanism
